moved_since.head: bb15526
moved_since.what: 32 commits. Eight translated READMEs and their own product; the one that mattered here is mcp-scan/pytests/test_surrogate_sanitization.py with strip_surrogates behind it - a defect class this corpus had no procedure for, now LOC-16. The product's detection capability did not move in a way the 2026-08-22 measurement misses.

products.note: weak-model precision round and the four-arm re-pool

moved_since.head: 27467b3
moved_since.what: 66 files. reference/evals/ gains run_eval.py, stage_agents.py, a deduplicator_agent and a ninth dataset; the sandbox layer becomes reference/core/environments/ with four backends; two more skills. Deepens the two axes already declared in docs/competitive-analysis.md rather than opening a third. Their two comparable stage datasets were read on 2026-09-01: a seven-substring no-model stub scores 10/10 on them, and the blind separability probe cannot clear them at n=6 and n=4, so it reports 2. Their granularity is now answered by gate-stage-eval-floor.sh rather than copied; neither product was re-run. Their mantis-dedupe/SKILL.md was read in full at 27467b3 on 2026-09-01: a three-tier ladder - exact anchors, a five-line root-cause normalisation, then vector embeddings via vertex_ai/gemini-embedding-001 with merge at cosine >=0.90 and distinct at <0.70. Three things are right in it and were adopted as reasoning, not copied: a signature promotes a pair to candidate and never decides alone, same file plus different line is DISTINCT, and possible_duplicate_of is a soft non-terminal state. Three holes: the 0.70-0.90 band has no written rule, Tier 3 spends a third party's API credits on every pair compared (safety contract rule 9), and the decision is a cosine - it never asks whether one fix closes both. Ours is DUP-01..DUP-06 in triage.md, deterministic, zero credits, and the unresolved band is the default rather than a gap.

MIT, created 2026-06-16. The closest product in the field by construction: a deterministic zero-dependency engine builds a cross-file link-graph and enumerates candidate source->sink taint paths, correlates several external scanners into one issue, ranks by EPSS/KEV/CVSS, and the model does the judging and an adversarial verification pass in which an uncertain high-severity stays `needs-human`. Found by competitive-discovery.sh on 2026-09-01 with ZERO stars - a popularity floor would have hidden it. Read on 2026-09-01: src/coverage.ts scores a pluggable-standard coverage matrix FROM the findings, with `unexamined` as a real state and failed scanners rendered as coverage loss. Its hole is that `engineCovers` is computed from kinds present anywhere in the run, so a category is credited by the engine's capability and never by what was read - there is no denominator. See docs/competitive-analysis.md. STILL NOT BENCHMARKED: reading a design is not measuring a product.
Semgrep/CodeQL discovery plus LLM verification - the same two-stage shape as this corpus's tooling-then-VER-09 pass, at a fraction of the size.
Autonomous offensive agent: plans engagements, runs recon, chains exploits. Same class of product, opposite posture - this corpus is defensive by contract and does not chain exploits.
Autonomous offensive agent for red-team operations. Same note as akira on posture.
Structured security audits with remediation plans, as a Claude Code skill. 32 stars and the most direct name-level competitor; last pushed 2026-02-10.
Prose skill suite with its own scoring engine and quality reviewer - a self-evaluation layer worth reading. Pushed once, on the day it was created.

CC-BY-SA-4.0, created 2026-01-14, 7,033 stars: a professional audit firm's own Claude Code skills for security research, vulnerability detection and audit workflows. The largest product in this lane and the reason `controls` exists - five text queries returned 39 repositories on 2026-09-10 and none of them was this one, because its name is `skills` and text search ranks on the name. discovery.$comment: The lane, so that something can ask whether the product list is still the field. competitive-freshness.sh re-checks the pins; nothing re-opened the set until 2026-09-01, when three of these queries returned maxgfr/ultrasec - MIT, in this exact lane, pushed two days earlier - and the baseline had never heard of it. Zero stars, which is why the bar is a skill marker and not popularity.
discovery.$comment_topic_queries: Text search ranks on a repository's name and description, so a product owned by an organisation and named `skills` is unreachable by every phrasing of this lane. Measured 2026-09-10: the five text queries above returned 39 distinct repositories and none was trailofbits/skills (7,033 stars, Claude Code skills for vulnerability detection and audit workflows, CC-BY-SA-4.0) or cloudflare/security-audit-skill (3,267 stars, MIT). A topic is metadata the owner sets rather than prose a ranker reads, which is why this lane is swept both ways. The ordering is by stars INSIDE one topic query's limit and decides who is looked at first, never who counts: the marker is still the bar, and the text queries are not star-ordered, so the zero-star tail stays reachable.
discovery.$comment_controls: Known positives the sweep must return. Every one of them is already resolved in `products` below, so this asks nothing about quality: it asks whether the instrument can still see a thing it is pointed at. A missing control takes the run to rc 2 and outranks an unresolved candidate, because an unresolved name is a fact about the list and an unseen control is a fact about the instrument that produced the list. Each `found_by` is the query that returned it when the control was written, measured on 2026-09-10 - it is what to repair when the control goes missing, not a promise that only that query can find it.

controls.why: org-owned, generically named, 7,033 stars, and invisible to every text query in this lane - the case that motivated the controls
MIT, a skill in this exact lane, and the five text queries in place on 2026-09-10 did not return it
the first-party security review action for the same host - if this lane cannot see it, the lane is not being read
zero stars, and the product that motivated competitive-discovery.sh - it is the control that proves the bar is not popularity

discovery.$comment_markers: Matched against the TOP LEVEL of the default branch's tree, one API call per candidate. `skills` catches a nested SKILL.md, which is how ultrasec ships.
discovery.$comment_queries: `vulnerability triage LLM agent` was the third query on the first run and returned zero hits, which took the whole run to rc 2 - correctly: a dead query is not a closed field. It was replaced by `vulnerability triage agent`, which returns 8. Every query here was checked to return results on 2026-09-01; one that stops doing so is a finding about the query, and the check will say so rather than pass.
discovery.$comment_cap: 7 text queries + 2 topic queries = 9 sweeps x per_query 8 = 72 hits at most, so the cap cannot be reached before the queries are exhausted. It is a cost ceiling on API calls, not a quality threshold, and it is written with the arithmetic so raising it is never a judgement call: raise per_query or either query list and this follows. gate-discovery-controls.sh recomputes this product and fails if the cap could bite first, so the arithmetic cannot drift out of the comment silently.

$comment_declined: Declining is a first-class answer and costs one line. What a candidate may not be is unnamed: an unresolved hit fails competitive-discovery.sh. A reason here is a claim about KIND, not about quality - nothing in this file says a declined product is worse.

declined.reason: Different target class: SWC vulnerabilities in smart contracts. Out of this corpus's lane by construction, not by quality.
Faces the other way: it is about securing skills you install, not about auditing a target with one. Adjacent to AI-22, not a competitor to it.
Audits a skill BEFORE you install it - a supply-chain check on the agent's own tooling. Same reason as the guide above.

Faces the other way, at scale: it scans agent skill FILES for malicious patterns and prompt injection before you trust them. Same reason as RationalEyes/claude-skills-security-guide and joshphoenix1/skill-security-audit - a supply-chain check on the agent's own tooling, not an audit of a target. 16,898 stars, and declining it is a statement about kind and nothing else.
Same class as SkillSpector: a multi-layer checker for agent skill files. Faces the tooling, not the target.
A distribution channel for skills that advertises its own pre-install audit. The audited artefact is the skill being installed; the lane here is auditing somebody's application.
A curated list of security-first skills for another host, whose detection is aimed at prompt injection and supply chain IN skills. A list and a tooling check, not a product that audits a target.
Different target class: Solidity smart contracts. Same reason as dungnotnull/smart-contract-security-audit-agent-skill - out of this corpus's lane by construction, not by quality.

The same auto-generated cluster the declined pattern below covers, in its `claude-code-security` spelling rather than `claude-skills-security`, so the pattern does not match it. Named one by one on purpose: a pattern is written when a count justifies it, and widening an existing one to swallow a second spelling is how a pattern quietly starts eating the lane.

$comment_declined_patterns: A pattern decline exists because a per-repo line for an auto-generated cluster is the way a check becomes noise and stops being read. It is narrow, it carries the count it covered when written, and the run reports how many each one absorbs - a pattern that starts eating the lane is visible rather than silent.

declined_patterns.reason: A cluster of auto-generated repositories, every one 'derived from' somebody else's skills list, all pushed on 2026-04-28 under different unrelated owner names. They are republications of a list, not products, and their star counts (38-51) are the reason the bar for this check is a skill marker and never popularity.
